title: The Neighbor I Visit Without Telling Anyone
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] There is an elderly man who lives two doors down from me, and for the past year, I have been visiting him twice a week.
Narrator: [reflective] His children moved abroad long ago, and although they call occasionally, he spends most of his days completely alone in that quiet house.
Narrator: [honestly] I started visiting almost by accident, after I noticed his newspaper piling up uncollected by the gate for several days in a row.
Narrator: [gently] At first, I only knocked to check if he was alright, but eventually those short visits turned into something closer to a habit I looked forward to.
Narrator: [thoughtful] If someone asked my wife what I do on Tuesday and Friday evenings, she genuinely wouldn't know how to answer in detail.
Narrator: [honestly] I never mentioned it to her, not because I'm hiding anything shameful, but because explaining it out loud would somehow make it feel smaller.
Narrator: [reflective] Even my closest friends assume those evenings are simply my time for errands, and I've never bothered correcting that assumption.
Narrator: [with feeling] Sometimes we just sit together in silence, drinking tea, while he tells the same three stories about his youth that I've already heard many times.
Narrator: [warmly] I don't mind hearing them again, though, because his face changes completely whenever he talks about those years, as if he becomes younger while speaking.
Narrator: [thoughtful] A colleague once suggested I post about it online, arguing it might inspire other people to check on their own elderly neighbors.
Narrator: [honestly] I understood his point, and perhaps it really would encourage someone else, but something about the suggestion still felt wrong to me.
Narrator: [reflective] If I photographed those visits for others to see, I suspect I would start visiting partly for the photograph, without even realizing the shift.
Narrator: [sincere] So instead, I keep it quiet, unrecorded, and mostly unmentioned, even though nobody would think less of me for sharing it.
Narrator: [peacefully] As long as he keeps opening that door glad to see me, I don't need anyone else to know these evenings ever happened at all.

quiz.question: How did the narrator first start visiting his elderly neighbor?
options: He noticed the newspaper piling up uncollected by the gate
quiz.explanation: He started after noticing the newspaper piling up uncollected by the gate for several days.

quiz.question: Why hasn't the narrator told his wife the details of his Tuesday and Friday evenings?
options: Explaining it out loud would somehow make it feel smaller
His wife told him not to mention it
quiz.explanation: He says it's not because he's hiding anything shameful, but explaining it out loud would make it feel smaller.

quiz.question: What do the narrator and the elderly man usually do during visits?
options: Sit in silence drinking tea while the man repeats old stories
quiz.explanation: They sit together drinking tea while the man tells the same three stories about his youth.

quiz.question: What did a colleague suggest the narrator do?
options: Post about the visits online to inspire others
Charge the neighbor for his time
quiz.explanation: A colleague suggested posting about it online, arguing it might inspire others to check on elderly neighbors.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator reject that suggestion?
options: He was too busy to post online
He suspected he would start visiting partly for the photograph
He thought no one would care
quiz.explanation: He suspected that if he photographed the visits, he would start visiting partly for the photograph without realizing it.
